articles.title: This Day in MMA August 20: McGregor vs Diaz UFC 202
articles.description: Ten years ago tonight, Conor McGregor and Nate Diaz went to war at UFC 202. Nate Diaz had submitted McGregor just six months earlier at UFC 196, handing the Irish superstar his first UFC loss. McGregor demanded the rematch at 170 pounds. What followed became one of the most memorable fights in UFC history. McGregor dropped Diaz three times early, but Diaz refused to go away. He rallied as the fight progressed, turning the third round into a war and pushing McGregor through all five rounds. McGregor ultimately won by majority decision, evening their rivalry at 1-1. After the fight, McGregor couldn’t help but respect Diaz’s toughness: 🗣️ “One man’s face was opened up and he’s still just coming. He’s still just coming. You’ve got to respect that. You’ve got to respect Nate and the style of fighting that he brings. How can you not?” Diaz, however, never believed he’d lost. 🗣️ “I didn’t think for a second that I lost.” August 20, 2016 → August 20, 2026. Ten years later, Conor McGregor and Nate Diaz remain tied 1-1 — and MMA fans are still waiting for the trilogy. articles.title: Beating Ian Garry Does NOT Make Islam the GOAT
articles.description: Is Islam Makhachev really the greatest mixed martial artist of all time, or are we once again handing out GOAT status immediately after a big UFC main event? Chael Sonnen questions why the GOAT conversation around Islam exploded after his victory over Ian Machado Garry. If beating Garry is the accomplishment that pushed Islam over the top, what does that say about Shavkat Rakhmonov, who also defeated Garry while maintaining an undefeated record? Then there's Jon Jones. Chael argues that any greatest-of-all-time discussion becomes extremely difficult when Jones' career exists, particularly when we've never definitively established the weaknesses an opponent could exploit. Chael also compares Islam's approach as champion with Alexander Volkanovski's willingness to fight whoever has earned the opportunity, whenever and wherever the fight is offered. Islam deserves enormous respect for everything he's accomplished, but Chael isn't ready to crown him based on one more win. articles.title: Carlos Prates Says He’s Fighting Islam Next
articles.description: Carlos Prates says he's been told he's next for Islam Makhachev and that a new eight-fight UFC deal came with a welterweight title opportunity. But Chael Sonnen isn't convinced the situation is that simple. Michael Morales appeared to be positioned for the same opportunity. After his win at Madison Square Garden, there were reports that Dana White told Morales he was next, and Morales was subsequently selected as the backup fighter for Islam's championship fight with Ian Machado Garry. Historically, Chael points out, successfully serving as a UFC title-fight backup has usually led to the next championship opportunity. So where does that leave Prates? Chael understands why fans love Carlos Prates, but questions the assumption that he's clearly more popular than Morales and can't overlook Prates' loss to Ian Garry. Most importantly, Chael doesn't want Prates and Morales fighting each other and eliminating one future challenger. articles.title: Has Islam Earned the Right to Be Above Ilia?#ufc
articles.description: How can Islam Makhachev be ranked ahead of Ilia Topuria? That's the question Chael Sonnen is asking. After Ilia's latest loss, the two fighters now have something important in common: one career loss and one stoppage loss. But Chael argues that the circumstances surrounding those losses matter. Ilia's loss came in a massive main event on the White House lawn against elite competition. Islam's only loss came much earlier in his career. So does recency really change the argument? Chael also brings up something Islam doesn't particularly enjoy discussing: Islam turned down a fight with Ilia. To be fair, Islam had a reason. He argued that Ilia hadn't fought at lightweight yet and wanted him to establish himself at 155 pounds before fighting the champion. But Chael points out that Islam himself had previously made similar moves when other fighters challenged him. Now there's another issue. When asked about potential opponents like Michael Morales and Benoît Saint Denis, Islam's answer was essentially: have them fight each other. Chael's question is whether that eventually becomes another form of avoiding a direct challenge. Because if you're going to call someone the greatest fighter in the world, what happens when that fighter starts saying no to fights? Is Islam still clearly ahead of Ilia? Or is the gap between them much smaller than people think? #IslamMakhachev #IliaTopuria #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #IslamVsIlia #UFCGOAT #CombatSports

articles.title: Ian Garry Was Too Focused on Islam’s Approval #ufc
articles.description: Ian Garry didn't lose because he lacked skill. Chael Sonnen believes the bigger issue was mindset. Throughout the fight, Chael saw Garry repeatedly seeking Islam Makhachev's approval instead of treating him like the man standing between him and a UFC championship. Garry praised Islam as the greatest fighter in the world. He continued reaching out to him between rounds and after the fight. Meanwhile, Islam was telling him to stop talking. For Chael, that's the problem. When you're fighting someone at this level, respect is one thing. But you're not there to make your opponent like you. You're there to take the championship from him. Chael believes Garry didn't behave like a young fighter who had come into the Octagon prepared to take the title by force. And that's especially important when you're losing rounds. Once a round is gone, you can't get it back. There is no reason to spend that time worrying about how the other team perceives you. The comparison to the famous Khabib-Conor McGregor rivalry makes the point even stronger. Chael wonders whether Garry was expecting some kind of mutual respect or acknowledgment after the fight instead of approaching it like a championship fight where only one man gets what he came for. Garry showed plenty of skill and toughness. But Chael believes he needs to overcome one thing moving forward: Stop worrying about being liked. Start believing you belong at the top. #IanGarry #IslamMakhachev #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #UFCChampionship #IanGarryUFC #CombatSports

articles.title: Why Did Islam Makhachev Wear Two Belts?
articles.description: Why is Islam Makhachev walking around with two UFC championship belts? Chael Sonnen looks at the photos of Islam following his welterweight title win and explains an important distinction: being a champion in two divisions is not the same thing as being a simultaneous “champ champ.” Islam was previously the UFC lightweight champion, but he gave up that title before becoming welterweight champion. So why does he have two belts? Chael goes back to Conor McGregor becoming a true simultaneous two-division champion against Eddie Alvarez, including the wild story of the UFC borrowing Tyron Woodley’s belt when they realized Conor needed a second one in the Octagon. He also uses Ilia Topuria and the BMF title to explain why actually winning a belt under the terms of a championship fight matters. The larger issue is how UFC history gets recorded. Winning a championship, defending a championship and reclaiming a championship are different accomplishments. If we're going to talk about champions and their legacies, Chael argues we should get the history right. articles.title: Why Is Islam Makhachev Asking Them to Fight?
articles.description: Islam Makhachev sits atop the UFC welterweight division with two viable challengers emerging in Michael Morales and Carlos Prates. So why is the champion suggesting they fight each other? Chael Sonnen examines Islam’s unusual approach to the contenders waiting behind him. After watching Ian Machado Garry offer specific resistance to Islam, Chael says the Michael Morales matchup suddenly became much more interesting. Carlos Prates brings another compelling option with power, personality and a style fans want to see. But instead of picking one, Islam suggested Morales and Prates fight each other. Chael questions what that means for Islam’s immediate future. If the UFC makes that fight, the process of determining a winner, recovery, another training camp and promotion could leave the champion waiting for months. articles.title: Ian Garry Was Too Nice to Islam #ufc
articles.description: Ian Garry fought well against Islam Makhachev. But Chael Sonnen believes there was one mental mistake Garry may eventually regret. According to Chael, Garry spent too much time trying to be liked by Islam instead of treating him like the obstacle standing between him and a UFC championship. The pep talks during the fight. The praise between rounds. The post-fight respect. Even telling people that Islam is the greatest fighter in the world. Chael's question is simple: Why are you trying to make this guy feel good? This was Garry's first UFC title fight, and Chael understands that he's still a young fighter learning how to handle the biggest moments of his career. But he believes there may come a point, weeks after the fight, when Garry looks back and wishes he had trusted himself more. Because the assignment was clear: get up. And Garry understood it. He repeatedly scrambled, fought to return to his feet, and showed the wrestling IQ and determination needed to compete with Islam's control game. That matters. Chael isn't criticizing Garry's performance. He's questioning the mindset surrounding it. You don't have to hate your opponent. But when you're fighting for the world championship, you have to believe you're better than the man standing across from you. Did Ian Garry show too much respect for Islam? #IanGarry #IslamMakhachev #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #UFCFight #IanGarryUFC #CombatSports

articles.title: Islam Looked Unbeatable… #ufc
articles.description: Is Islam Makhachev actually unbeatable? Chael Sonnen isn't ready to say yes. Ian Garry didn't expose a clear weakness in Islam's game, but he may have shown that a weakness could exist. Despite facing moments that could have frustrated a normal fighter, Islam stayed composed, handled the pressure, and performed at an extremely high level. Daniel Cormier also pointed out just how much was riding on this fight. Islam wasn't simply defending his reputation — he was fighting under the pressure of potentially breaking Anderson Silva's historic UFC win-streak record. And somehow, Islam still looked incredibly complete. But now Chael is looking at a new name: Michael Morales. Before this fight, the idea of Morales fighting Islam wasn't particularly compelling to Chael. Now it is. Why? Morales may be able to defend takedowns more effectively than Garry. He's explosive, dangerous, and brings serious power. Chael isn't claiming Morales is a better striker than Ian Garry — but he believes Morales may hit harder. If Morales can force Islam to work in areas where Garry couldn't, could he become the first fighter to genuinely expose a hole in Islam's game? Islam may still be the favorite. But for the first time, Chael sees a matchup that makes him genuinely curious. Islam Makhachev vs. Michael Morales just got interesting. #IslamMakhachev #MichaelMorales #IanGarry #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #IslamMakhachevUFC #CombatSports

articles.title: Ian Garry Has a BIG Problem
articles.description: Ian Machado Garry lost the UFC 330 main event to Islam Makhachev. Then he said something in the aftermath that matters more than the decision did. Chael Sonnen starts where everyone else is starting — what happens to the welterweight division now. Carlos Prates has a case. Michael Morales is undefeated. Islam has said he'll take the winner of the two. And nobody is asking the question underneath all of it: does Ian Machado Garry get to walk straight back onto the path to a world title? Then Chael gets to the part nobody is talking about. Garry brought up his age and immediately turned it into a reason he still has time. He tattooed the number 15 on his body because that was his first ranking. And backstage, he pulled Michael Morales aside to tell him he doesn't need to talk like that. Chael takes all three of those and shows you what they have in common. This isn't a recap. It's about urgency, and why the men who actually become champions don't believe there's a next time. Chael brings in Tom Brands at the University of Iowa, telling an Olympic hopeful with years left that his career ends this season — and why a coach would do that on purpose. articles.title: 🚨 Islam Makhachev REVEALS His Toughest Fight: “This Guy Is DOG!!!” 😳🔥
articles.description: After going five rounds with Ian Machado Garry at UFC 330, Islam Makhachev was asked the big question: 👀 Was Ian Garry the toughest opponent of his career? Islam says Garry belongs near the top: 👉 “Maybe top three, bro…” But one fight immediately came to mind — his first war with Alexander Volkanovski in Australia. 🔥 “The Australian fight was crazy. articles.title: Islam Makhachev STAYING at Welterweight "REAL FIGHTERS... TOUGHEST DIVISION" What's NEXT? | UFC 330
articles.description: Islam Makhachev says his future is officially at welterweight following his UFC 330 victory over Ian Machado Garry — and he already has an idea for determining his next challenger. After fighting the naturally bigger Garry for five rounds, Makhachev admitted that he still wants to add size and strength as he continues adjusting physically to 170 pounds. 💪 “I still have to try in some way to be bigger, more powerful. I have time.” But one thing Islam does NOT want to do is return to lightweight. Makhachev explained how much happier he is without having to endure the brutal weight cut to 155. 🔥 “I don’t want to go back to lightweight.” Islam says he’s now able to enjoy training with his team, his camp and even fight week rather than constantly battling the scale. “That’s why I will stay at welterweight and fight for many more years.” Islam also addressed the increasingly crowded welterweight title picture. Carlos Prates and Michael Morales were reportedly backstage arguing over which man deserves the next opportunity against Makhachev. Islam offered a simple solution: 🥊 LET THEM FIGHT EACH OTHER. “Maybe let them fight. Why don’t they fight to see who is the number one contender?” Makhachev says he’s actually excited about the dangerous contenders emerging at welterweight, specifically mentioning: 🔥 Carlos Prates 🔥 Michael Morales 🔥 Shavkat Rakhmonov Islam says having fighters like these waiting for him actually motivates him: “They make me train harder every day… these are the real fighters who can give me good fights.” Makhachev also believes welterweight presents an entirely different physical challenge than lightweight, calling 170 pounds the hardest and most powerful division in the UFC right now. As for his mentality after a difficult five-round fight with Garry? 🥶 “From the first minute to the last second, I’m going to war. I’m going to fight every second.” Islam Makhachev is staying at 170.
